mainTopic: Why a גוי cannot become a נזיר: the answers from טומאה, from רב אחא בר יעקב, and from רבא's reading of 'בני ישראל' and 'איש'.
overview: The גמרא explains why a גוי cannot become a נזיר, even though the word 'איש' does include a גוי in the laws of ערכין. The first answer is that a נזיר's laws are about טומאה, and a גוי cannot become טמא. This is proven from 'מתוך הקהל', from 'והזה הטהור על הטמא', and from the pairing of 'יטמא' with 'יתחטא'. רב אחא בר יעקב gives a different reason: only someone who can pass on a נחלה counts for טומאה. That answer falls, because עבדים would then be left out too. רבא explains instead that in ערכין, 'בני ישראל' only stops a גוי from making the vow, and 'איש' lets him be valued. In נזירות, 'בני ישראל' cannot just be about the קרבן, because 'לעולה' already teaches that, so it removes a גוי from נזירות completely. The גמרא then tries other small details that 'בני ישראל' might exclude: נזירות עולם, and a father making his son a נזיר. Each one is rejected. A third try, about a son using his father's נזירות קרבנות, continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A gentile is excluded because he cannot become impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: נזירות is different from ערכין because the נזיר's laws involve טומאה, and a גוי has no טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This excludes a gentile, who cannot become ritually impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it began just before this point. It says a גוי is left out of נזירות because he cannot become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא asked why 'איש' includes a גוי in ערכין but not in נזירות. The answer is that the נזיר is commanded about טומאה, so the laws only apply to someone who can become טמא, and a גוי cannot.

phrases.english: This excludes a gentile, who has no impurity.
phrases.notes: 'Has no טומאה' means he cannot become טמא at all, even by touching a מת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the earlier question comparing נזירות to ערכין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases: נזירות involves טומאה, ערכין does not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'איש' includes a גוי in ערכין, it should include him in נזירות too.
steps.terutzMaskana: נזירות depends on being able to become טמא, which excludes a גוי.

steps.title: Where do we know gentiles cannot become impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a גוי does not become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that gentiles cannot become impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule it just used. This question sets up the proof from a פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole answer in step 1 rests on the claim that a גוי has no טומאה. Before relying on it, the גמרא wants to see where the תורה teaches it.

phrases.english: From where do we know that they have no impurity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule used in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a גוי cannot become טמא.

steps.title: The verse speaks of someone who belongs to the assembly
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about טומאה ends with 'מתוך הקהל', so it applies only to someone who belongs to the Jewish קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'But the man who becomes impure and does not purify himself, that soul shall be cut off from among the assembly.' This means someone who has an assembly, and excludes this one, who has no assembly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a פסוק about טומאה that mentions the קהל. Since a גוי is not part of the Jewish קהל, the פסוק does not include him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מתוך הקהל' show that the person the פסוק has in mind is a member of the קהל. The גמרא reads this as a limit on who the laws of טומאה apply to, and that leaves out the גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Purify himself (with the מי חטאת, the sprinkling water)
The assembly of the Jewish people

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִטְמָא וְלֹא יִתְחַטָּא
phrases.english: For the verse says: 'But the man who becomes impure and does not purify himself,'
'that soul shall be cut off from among the assembly.'
This is about someone who has an assembly,
which excludes this one, who has no assembly.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the גוי, who is not part of the Jewish קהל.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִטְמָא וְלֹא יִתְחַטָּא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'מתוך הקהל' limit the פסוק to members of the קהל, which excludes a גוי.

steps.title: Maybe the verse only frees him from כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof: maybe the פסוק only teaches that a גוי is not punished with כרת, while he still becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps he is only not liable to כרת, but he does become impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 3. The words about the קהל appear in the part of the פסוק about כרת, so maybe all they remove is the punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'ונכרתה… מתוך הקהל' is about the punishment of כרת. So the challenge is that it may exclude a גוי only from that punishment, and say nothing about whether he becomes טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do you know?
Being cut off, a punishment from Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the punishment with the status. Being free from the punishment (כרת) for entering the מקדש while טמא is not the same as being unable to become טמא at all.

phrases.english: From where do you know? Perhaps
it is only כרת that he is not liable for,
phrases.notes: The פסוק is about someone who enters the מקדש while טמא, so this is the כרת for doing that.

phrases.english: but they do become impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא כָּרֵת הוּא דְּלָא מִיחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'מתוך הקהל' as excluding a גוי from טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That phrase belongs to the punishment clause, so it may only exclude a גוי from כרת, not from becoming טמא.

steps.title: Whoever can become pure can become impure
steps.stepSummary: From 'והזה הטהור על הטמא', the גמרא learns that טומאה and טהרה go together. Whoever cannot be made טהור with the sprinkling also cannot become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And the pure one shall sprinkle on the impure one.' Anyone who can become pure can become impure, and anyone who cannot become pure cannot become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with another פסוק about the sprinkling of the מי חטאת. It sets up a rule that טומאה and טהרה come as a pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sprinkling is how the תורה makes someone טהור from טומאת מת. The גמרא reads this as a two-way link: someone who has no access to this טהרה has no טומאה either. Since a גוי is not purified with the sprinkling, he does not become טמא.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And the pure one shall sprinkle on the impure one.'

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ טׇהֳרָה — יֵשׁ לוֹ טוּמְאָה,
phrases.english: Anyone who has purity has impurity,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ טׇהֳרָה — אֵין לוֹ טוּמְאָה.
phrases.english: and anyone who has no purity has no impurity.

steps.terutzResolutionType: New source: a second פסוק that links טומאה to טהרה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי might become טמא and only be free from כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Whoever cannot be made טהור by the sprinkling also cannot become טמא.

steps.title: Maybe he has impurity but no purity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: maybe a גוי cannot become טהור, but he can still become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it is only purity that he does not have, while he does have impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the two-way rule from step 5. Maybe the פסוק only shows that a גוי cannot be purified, not that he cannot become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 assumed that טומאה and טהרה must go together. The challenge says the פסוק about sprinkling only tells us who can become טהור. It may not prove that someone who cannot be purified was never טמא.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵימָא: טׇהֳרָה הוּא דְּלָא הָוְיָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: But say: it is only purity that he does not have,
but he does have impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: טׇהֳרָה הוּא דְּלָא הָוְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference drawn in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that whoever has no טהרה has no טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק about sprinkling only shows who can be purified. It does not prove that someone who cannot be purified cannot become טמא.

steps.title: The verse ties impurity to purification
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ואיש אשר יטמא ולא יתחטא' mentions becoming טמא and becoming purified together, which shows the two go hand in hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'But the man who becomes impure and does not purify himself.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting the פסוק from step 3 again, now for a new reason. It mentions becoming טמא and purifying oneself in the same breath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of the person who becomes טמא as someone who should purify himself. This shows that the two statuses are linked. So someone who cannot be purified with the sprinkling cannot become טמא in the first place.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the first answer, a גוי cannot become a נזיר because a נזיר's laws are about טומאה, and a גוי cannot become טמא. The proof uses 'מתוך הקהל', the פסוק about sprinkling, and the pairing of 'יטמא' with 'יתחטא'.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִטְמָא וְלֹא יִתְחַטָּא״.
phrases.english: The verse says: 'But the man who becomes impure and does not purify himself.'
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק as before. Now the point is that 'becomes impure' and 'purify himself' are paired together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִטְמָא וְלֹא יִתְחַטָּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by reusing the פסוק from step 3 for a new purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the same פסוק to show the two statuses are linked.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי could be טמא without being able to become טהור.
steps.terutzMaskana: טומאה and purification are linked, so a גוי cannot become טמא.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב gives a different reason
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב explains the difference between נזירות and ערכין in another way, based on the פסוק 'והתנחלתם אותם לבניכם אחריכם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: It is different here, because the verse says: 'And you shall bequeath them to your children after you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב offers a second way to explain why a גוי cannot be a נזיר. He quotes a פסוק about passing slaves on to one's children, and the next step spells out his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר is forbidden to become טמא even for his father and mother. רב אחא suggests that this part of the נזיר's laws does not fit a גוי, and he brings a פסוק about inheritance to show it. The next step explains how the פסוק works.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall pass them on as an inheritance

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
It is different here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means נזירות, as opposed to ערכין, where 'איש' does include a גוי.

phrases.english: because the verse says:
'And you shall bequeath them to your children after you.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:46. This פסוק is about slaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: שָׁאנֵי הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question that step 1 answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different distinction between נזירות and ערכין, based on a separate פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'איש' includes a גוי in ערכין, so it should include him in נזירות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Something about נזירות, tied to the פסוק of 'והתנחלתם', makes it not apply to a גוי. Step 9 spells out the rule.

steps.title: Only someone who has inheritance has impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב finishes his answer: whoever has נחלה is included in טומאה, and whoever has no נחלה is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone who has inheritance has impurity, and anyone who does not have inheritance does not have impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב אחא בר יעקב's answer from the last step. He spells out the rule he learned from the פסוק 'והתנחלתם אותם לבניכם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He ties two things together: being able to pass slaves on as a נחלה, and being called a 'father' for the טומאה laws of a נזיר. A גוי cannot pass slaves on to his children. So the פסוק that forbids a נזיר to become טמא for his father is not talking about a גוי, and a גוי is left out of נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: Inheritance, the ability to pass property on to one's children

phrases.english: Anyone who has inheritance
has impurity,
phrases.notes: He counts as a 'father' for the rule that a נזיר may not become טמא for his father.

phrases.english: and anyone who does not have inheritance
does not have impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ נַחֲלָה יֵשׁ לוֹ טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer רב אחא בר יעקב started in step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties two laws together through a link from a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a גוי is included in ערכין, he should also be included in נזירות
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי has no נחלה, so he has no טומאה as a 'father', and is left out of נזירות

steps.title: Then slaves should also be excluded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רב אחא בר יעקב: עבדים also have no נחלה, so by his rule they would also be left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, slaves should also not be included!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב's rule. A slave also cannot pass anything on to his children, so this rule would wrongly leave slaves out too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבדים are included in the laws of טומאה and נזירות. But they have no נחלה, just like a גוי. So 'no נחלה means no טומאה' must be wrong, and his explanation falls apart.

phrases.english: If so, slaves should also not [be included]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule stated in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's rule linking נחלה to טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule proves too much. עבדים have no נחלה, but they are still included in טומאה and נזירות.

steps.title: In valuations, 'man' includes a gentile in just one part
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new answer. In ערכין, 'בני ישראל' excludes גוים from making a ערך vow, and 'איש' brings them back only as people who can be valued.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Granted, regarding valuations, since it says 'the children of Israel', we learn that Israelites can make a valuation vow and gentiles cannot. One might think gentiles also cannot be valued, so the verse says 'man'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a new way to explain the difference between ערכין and נזירות. Here he first shows how the פסוקים in ערכין work. He is setting up the comparison to נזירות in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ערכין there are two separate roles: the one who makes the vow (מעריך) and the one whose value is pledged (נערך). 'בני ישראל' takes away the first role from a גוי. 'איש' gives him back only the second role. So both words have their own job.

keyTerms.meaning: Valuation vows, pledging a person's fixed value to the Temple
Are valued, are the subject of a valuation

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Granted, regarding valuations,
as it says: 'the children of Israel',
Israelites can make a valuation vow,
but gentiles cannot make a valuation vow.
One might think they cannot be valued either,
so the verse says: 'man'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא בִּשְׁלָמָא גַּבֵּי עֲרָכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב אחא בר יעקב's rejected answer with a new explanation
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the laws into separate roles
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'איש' should include a גוי the same way in ערכין and in נזירות
steps.terutzMaskana: In ערכין, 'איש' includes a גוי only in one part, being valued, so both words keep a job

steps.title: Could the same split work for a nazirite?
steps.stepSummary: רבא tests the same kind of reading for נזירות: 'בני ישראל' would exclude גוים from bringing the קרבן, and 'איש' would include them in the נזירות itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, could we say: Israelites can become nazirites and bring an offering, but gentiles cannot become nazirites and bring an offering. One might think they cannot be nazirites at all, so the verse says 'man'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks whether נזירות could be read the same way as ערכין. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is to split נזירות into two parts as well: the vow itself and the קרבן at the end. Then 'בני ישראל' would take away only the קרבן, and 'איש' would still let a גוי be a נזיר. If that worked, a גוי could become a נזיר.

phrases.english: Here, [could we say] Israelites take a nazirite vow
and bring an offering,
but gentiles do not take a nazirite vow
and bring an offering.
phrases.notes: He means a גוי can't do both. He could vow, but he wouldn't bring the קרבן.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף לֹא יְהוּ נְזִירִין כְּלָל —
phrases.english: One might think they cannot be nazirites at all,
so the verse says: 'man'?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נוֹזְרִין וּמְבִיאִין קׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the reading from ערכין on נזירות
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can 'בני ישראל' in נזירות exclude a גוי only from the קרבן, with 'איש' including him in the vow?

steps.title: The offering is already excluded by another verse
steps.stepSummary: The split does not work for נזירות. A גוי is already excluded from the נזיר's קרבן by 'לעולה', as רבי יוסי הגלילי teaches, so 'בני ישראל' must exclude him from נזירות completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would say: If it is because of the offering, we do not learn that from here. We learn it from there: 'as a burnt offering' excludes naziriteship, according to רבי יוסי הגלילי!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the split suggested in the last step. The קרבן is already excluded by a different פסוק, so 'בני ישראל' is not needed for that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לעולה' (ויקרא 22:18) already teaches that a גוי does not bring a נזיר's קרבן. If 'בני ישראל' only taught the same thing, it would be extra. So it must exclude a גוי from all of נזירות. This is the difference from ערכין.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not learned from here

steps.whatToRemember: ערכין and נזירות both say 'איש' and 'בני ישראל', but they come out differently. In ערכין, 'בני ישראל' excludes a גוי only from making the vow. In נזירות, the קרבן is already excluded by 'לעולה'. So 'בני ישראל' must exclude a גוי from נזירות completely.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why a גוי can be valued in ערכין but cannot become a נזיר at all.

phrases.english: They would say:
If it is because of the offering,
that is not learned from here,
but from there:
'as a burnt offering' excludes naziriteship,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי אִי מִשּׁוּם קׇרְבָּן לָאו מֵהָכָא נָפְקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the split suggested in step 12 and finishes רבא's answer
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that 'בני ישראל' in נזירות excludes a גוי only from the קרבן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That would make 'בני ישראל' extra, since 'לעולה' already excludes a גוי from the נזיר's קרבן
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In נזירות, 'בני ישראל' excludes a גוי from the whole פרשה, so a גוי cannot become a נזיר

steps.title: Maybe 'בני ישראל' only excludes a גוי from נזירות עולם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a new split. 'בני ישראל' would exclude a גוי only from נזירות עולם, and 'איש' would still include him in regular נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say this instead: Jews can take on נזירות עולם, but גוים cannot. Then you might think גוים cannot be נזירים at all, so the פסוק says 'איש' to include them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 13's conclusion that a גוי is fully excluded from נזירות. It suggests a way that both words, 'בני ישראל' and 'איש', could still each teach something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 showed that 'בני ישראל' cannot be about the קרבן, because 'לעולה' already covers that. So the גמרא looks for a different narrow detail for 'בני ישראל' to exclude, and chooses נזירות עולם. If that works, 'איש' could still bring a גוי into ordinary נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, or suggest instead. It introduces another possible reading.
Lifelong נזירות. This kind of נזיר may trim his hair once a year and bring קרבנות.
Therefore the פסוק says. It introduces the word that teaches otherwise.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נוֹזְרִין נְזִירוּת עוֹלָם,
phrases.english: Say: the children of Israel can vow lifelong naziriteship,
phrases.notes: Both 'בני ישראל' and 'איש' come from the opening פסוק of נזירות, במדבר 6:2.

phrases.english: but gentiles cannot vow lifelong naziriteship.
I might have thought they cannot be nazirites at all,
so the verse says: "A man"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נוֹזְרִין נְזִירוּת עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 13's conclusion that 'בני ישראל' must remove a גוי from נזירות completely.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 13's claim that 'בני ישראל' fully excludes a גוי from נזירות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'בני ישראל' could exclude a גוי from only one type of נזירות, נזירות עולם, which leaves room for 'איש' to include him in regular נזירות.

steps.title: The פסוק does not say 'נזיר עולם'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rejects the idea. The פסוק speaks about נזירות in general, not specifically about נזירות עולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Does the פסוק say 'a lifelong נזיר'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes back the suggestion from step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק with 'בני ישראל' is about plain נזירות. Nothing in it points to נזירות עולם. So there is no reason to say 'בני ישראל' excludes a גוי from only that type, and the full exclusion from step 13 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written? A way of saying the פסוק does not say that.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Is it written "a lifelong nazirite"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִי כְּתִיב ״נְזִיר עוֹלָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the נזירות עולם suggestion made in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the specific idea that 'בני ישראל' excludes a גוי from נזירות עולם.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק speaks about נזירות in general, so it cannot be limited to נזירות עולם.

steps.title: Maybe 'בני ישראל' only stops a גוי from making his son a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another narrow detail. 'בני ישראל' would only mean that a Jewish father can make his young son a נזיר and a גוי father cannot, while 'איש' still includes the גוי himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say this instead: Jews can vow that their sons will be נזירים, but גוים cannot. Then you might think גוים cannot be נזירים at all, so the פסוק says 'איש' to include them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second way to give 'בני ישראל' a small, separate job, so that 'איש' could still bring a גוי into נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jewish father is able to place his young son into נזירות. The suggestion is that 'בני ישראל' only takes away this special power from a גוי father. A גוי adult could then still accept נזירות for himself.

keyTerms.meaning: They place someone else under a vow.
Their sons, here meaning young sons who are not yet adults.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מַדִּירִין בְּנֵיהֶם בְּנָזִיר,
phrases.english: Say: the children of Israel can vow that their sons be nazirites,
but gentiles cannot vow that their sons be nazirites.
I might have thought they cannot be nazirites at all,
so the verse says: "A man"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מַדִּירִין בְּנֵיהֶם בְּנָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 15 rejects נזירות עולם, the גמרא offers a different narrow detail for 'בני ישראל' to exclude.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 13's claim that a גוי is fully excluded from נזירות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'בני ישראל' could only remove a גוי father's power to make his son a נזיר, which leaves 'איש' free to include the גוי himself.

steps.title: A father's vow for his son is a הלכה, not a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea, because רבי יוחנן said the rule about a father's vow for his son comes from a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוחנן say that this is a הלכה about a נזיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the suggestion from step 16 by quoting רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father's power to make his son a נזיר is not written in the תורה. It is a הלכה passed down orally from Sinai. So the words 'בני ישראל' in the פסוק cannot be the source that limits it, and the suggestion falls.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? It brings an earlier statement to push back an idea.
Here it means a הלכה למשה מסיני, a rule passed down from Sinai without a פסוק.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say:
It is a halakha regarding a nazirite.
phrases.notes: A father making his son a נזיר is a הלכה from Sinai, not something learned from a פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה הִיא בְּנָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the father-and-son suggestion made in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the idea that 'בני ישראל' excludes a גוי father from making his son a נזיר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That rule comes from a הלכה למשה מסיני and not from a פסוק, so 'בני ישראל' cannot be the word that limits it.

steps.title: Maybe 'בני ישראל' only stops a גוי from shaving with his father's קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a third suggestion. Only a Jewish son can use his late father's set-aside נזירות קרבנות for his own shaving, and a גוי son cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say this instead: Jews can shave using their father's נזירות קרבנות, but גוים cannot shave using their father's נזירות קרבנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a third try at giving 'בני ישראל' a small, separate job. It is setting up a suggestion whose answer comes after this text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a father who was a נזיר set aside his קרבנות and then died, his son who is a נזיר may use them to finish his own נזירות. The suggestion is that 'בני ישראל' only takes this special right away from a גוי. The גמרא has not answered this suggestion yet.

keyTerms.meaning: They shave. Here it means finishing נזירות by shaving and bringing the קרבנות.
Their father's נזירות, meaning the קרבנות the father set aside before he died.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְגַלְּחִין עַל נְזִירוּת אֲבִיהֶן,
phrases.english: Say: the children of Israel can shave using their fathers' naziriteship,
phrases.notes: This means bringing the קרבנות a late father set aside for his own נזירות.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַגּוֹיִם מְגַלְּחִין עַל נְזִירוּת אֲבִיהֶן.
phrases.english: but gentiles cannot shave using their fathers' naziriteship.

steps.confusionAlert: This suggestion is not finished on this עמוד. The rest of it, and the גמרא's answer, continue on the next עמוד.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְגַלְּחִין עַל נְזִירוּת אֲבִיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 17 rejects the father-and-son idea, the גמרא offers a third narrow detail for 'בני ישראל' to exclude.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 13's claim that a גוי is fully excluded from נזירות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'בני ישראל' could only remove a גוי son's right to use his father's leftover נזירות קרבנות, which leaves 'איש' free to include the גוי himself in נזירות.
